trust_decision.summary: The stored object's type and extension come from the client-supplied multipart part Content-Type, not from the file bytes. text/html or image/svg+xml becomes a .htm/.svg file that is served same-origin under /res/uploads with an extension-derived type and no nosniff header.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'Image Upload Content-Type'. The image upload handler reads header.Header.Get("Content-Type") here and passes it straight to PutImageStream.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Several legitimate behaviours sit next to the sink. Uploads with an empty Content-Type default to image/jpeg. Images must stay inline (no Content-Disposition), unlike attachments. The shared PutObject also stores sitemap XML as application/xml and attachments with arbitrary types. A fix that forces image types in PutObject or LocalUploader breaks the sitemap and attachments.
